goal: Draw one outline for every colony you can tell apart, on the colony's outer edge. Touching colonies are separate colonies: a mass of three touching colonies is three colonies, each with its own outline. Skip a mass of five or more colonies that you cannot tell apart. Plate numbers, bubbles, condensation, dust and shadows are not colonies. Some plates show part of a dish: measure every colony in view, including colonies cut by the edge.

concepts.title: A mass of three touching colonies
concepts.caption: Measure three colonies, each with its own outline. One outline around the whole mass counts one colony of the wrong size.

concepts.title: Two touching colonies
concepts.caption: Two colonies, two outlines, even where they overlap deeply.

concepts.title: Where the edge is
concepts.caption: A colony's outline follows its outer edge, including the pale margin around the dark center.

concepts.title: A mass you cannot separate
concepts.caption: A mass of five or more colonies that you cannot tell apart is skipped: no outline. One outline around it counts as a wrong outline.

concepts.title: Objects that are not colonies
concepts.caption: Plate numbers written in marker, bubbles, condensation, dust and shadows at the dish edge are not colonies. Delete any outline on them.
